title: StreamCSD: SSD-Autonomous Stream Management via In-Storage Content Learning
problem: Write amplification from garbage collection during SSD operation degrades performance and shortens lifespan; existing stream management solutions require host-side changes, hindering adoption.
motivation: Multi-stream SSDs can reduce write amplification through semantic stream separation, but current approaches need OS/application modification. Autonomous in-SSD approaches could enable broader adoption.
method: StreamCSD measures how much data compresses within the SSD using built-in compression engines. It continuously groups data into separate streams based on compression similarity using streaming K-means—an algorithm that updates groupings as new data arrives. Because the SSD performs this work on its own, the host computer doesn't require any modifications.
key_novelty: StreamCSD is the first system to manage SSD data streams autonomously on the drive itself, using compression measurements to decide how to group data together.
contributions: Reduces write amplification from 1.7 to 1.06 on generative AI workloads
Matches state-of-the-art host-aware methods with host-side modifications
Minimal bandwidth overhead; no host modifications required
limitations: Not discussed; evaluation focuses on generative AI but applicability to other workloads unclear.
primary_theme: Autonomous SSD stream management via compression-based clustering
